Every dot is one $5 Starbucks coffee, every workday since 2000. 6,728 of them.

That's $33,640 at Starbucks. No judgement.

If every $5 had gone into Starbucks stock instead: $204,586 today.

The brightest dots are the very first coffees and the ones from the 2008 crash. The single best: January 4, 2000. That $5 coffee is $158.68 today.

You were standing in the store, buying the product instead of the company.

Split-adjusted SBUX, dividends not included.

Tag the friend who basically lives at Starbucks.

Follow for the next one. Every claim on here gets tested against a control.

Follow for a new chart every day.

Every dot is a day someone bought Costco stock, 7,113 of them from 1986 to 2014. Red means that buyer is losing money.

One day later: 48% are red.
Ten years: still 22 red.

At 10 years and 5 months, not one dot is losing.

The last red dot bought in February 2000, right at the top of the dot-com bubble, and was red for over 10 years. For Costco.

Every single person who waited made money.

Split-adjusted price, dividends excluded.
